text_blocks.snippet: Diabetic myopathy refers to muscle damage and dysfunction caused by diabetes. It encompasses a range of conditions including muscle inflammation, ischemia, and fatty atrophy, often associated with long-standing, poorly controlled diabetes. This can manifest as muscle pain, weakness, and reduced exercise capacity.
snippet_highlighted_words: muscle damage and dysfunction caused by diabetes

list.title: Muscle Damage:
list.snippet: Diabetic myopathy involves various types of muscle tissue damage, including inflammation, ischemia (reduced blood flow), hemorrhage, infarction (tissue death), necrosis, fibrosis (scarring), and fatty atrophy (muscle wasting).

list.title: Spectrum of Conditions:
list.snippet: It's not a single disease, but rather a collection of muscle-related complications arising from diabetes.

list.title: Prevalence:
list.snippet: While sometimes seen in younger individuals with diabetes, it's more common in those with long-standing, poorly managed diabetes, particularly those with complications like neuropathy (nerve damage).
